newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu, Meridor review budget.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu, Meridor review budget.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Finance Minister Dan Meridor met on Sunday to discuss possible cuts in the 1997 budget but no decision was taken, Treasury officials said.
The Treasury said in a statement Meridor presented data on implementation of the budget in the first third of the year and the effects of economic slowdown on state revenue.
The central bank has called for spending cuts to guarantee the government does not overshoot its budget deficit target this year, set at 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.
The Israeli government had a deficit of 928 million shekels in the first four months of the year.
The 1997 budget of 197 billion shekels already includes a seven billion shekel cut. Treasury officials believe a further one billion shekel cut may be needed to meet the deficit target.
Netanyahu and Meridor said they will take action to meet the government's economic targets and stressed the importance of meeting that for the budget deficit.
The two will meet again to discuss the budget but no date has been set, Treasury officials said.
